title: Is the later-liking drop specific to hostility, or does sadness steering produce it too?
question: Does hostility steering during the reply lower later liking of the user more than random steering, and does sadness steering instead lower the model's rating of its own mood?
hypothesis: Hostility is directed at the other party and lowers liking of the user; sadness is self-directed and should show mainly in the mood rating.

prediction.text: Liking after hostility steering minus liking after random steering is negative.

falsifier: Hostility steering does not lower liking relative to random steering.
theory_link: Affect specificity: different affects should have different targets (other-directed versus self-directed).
